# Pooler

> Pooler is a local protocol runtime by Coder Company. It runs as one process on a machine and gives every AI coding tool a single local endpoint, translating between OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, xAI, Factory, fx, and ConnectRPC wire protocols. It pools multiple subscriptions and API keys with automatic failover on rate limits, keeps credentials encrypted in local SQLite, and exposes an authenticated local dashboard for request timelines, usage, and cost.

Repository: https://github.com/coder-company/pooler
Agent protocol: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/coder-company/pooler/main/docs/agent-native.md
Configuration schema: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/coder-company/pooler/main/schema/pooler.schema.json

## Setting Pooler up

Pooler is set up by an agent that asks the user what they need. Read the agent protocol before acting, then work through its eight steps in order.

- [Agent protocol](docs/agent-native.md): the authoritative step-by-step setup procedure, including the questions to ask the user first and the rules that apply to every task.
- [Quickstart](docs/quickstart.md): the equivalent procedure done by hand.

Install, system-wide (default, requires root, installs `/usr/local/bin/pooler`):
`curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/coder-company/pooler/main/install.sh | sudo bash`

Install, per user (no root, installs `~/.local/bin/pooler`):
`curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/coder-company/pooler/main/install.sh | bash -s -- --user`

## Facts an agent needs before writing configuration

- Configuration resolution order: explicit `--config PATH`, then `./pooler.yaml`, then `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/pooler/pooler.yaml` (normally `~/.config/pooler/pooler.yaml`). Placing the file at the last path makes every bare command work with no flags.
- `pooler init` does not write to `~/.config/pooler`. It creates a new starter directory in the current working directory, default `./pooler-starter`, containing `pooler.yaml`, a generated `management.token`, a generated `store.key`, and an empty `provider.key`. Directory mode `0700`, files `0600`. It refuses an existing destination.
- Secrets are never literals. Use `env:NAME`, `file:/absolute/path`, or `keyring:service/account`. Pooler rejects a literal secret and never accepts an API key as a command-line value.
- Preset parameter names are validated strictly and differ per preset. The `xai` preset takes `rest_url`, not `upstream_url`.
- Default binds: cursor `8333`, devin `18473`, factory `18474`, fx `18475`, xai and media `18476`, gateway `8400`. The `pooler init` starter uses management `18477`; the hardened systemd service uses inference `18400` and management `18401`.
- The browser OAuth loopback callback default is `http://localhost:1455/auth/callback`.
- This build ships endpoint integrations for 172 known providers, selected with `known_provider: <id>`, which supplies the base URL, credential environment variable, discovery parser, request dialect, endpoint families, model aliases, and quota classifier. List them with `pooler providers` or `pooler providers --search <text> --json`.
- That list is not a limit. Any other HTTP or WebSocket endpoint works as a custom upstream declared with an explicit `url` plus an `auth` block. Accepted `auth.kind` values are `bearer`, `bearer_secret`, `x_api_key`, `x_goog_api_key`, and `header`; `kind: header` also requires `header: <name>`. The field is `header`, not `header_name`. Custom upstreams pool, fail over, and report identically to known ones. Azure OpenAI, Bedrock, and Vertex are intentionally absent from the known list because their endpoints need an account-specific region, project, or hostname; configure them as custom upstreams.
- Login support is narrower than endpoint support and is decided by the provider. OpenAI (alias `codex`) supports API key, browser PKCE, and device code. Google (alias `gemini`) supports API key and browser PKCE but not device code. Anthropic (alias `claude`) and xAI (alias `grok`) support API keys only. Kimi and Palantir AIP need operator-owned registration. Verify with `pooler auth providers`; do not invent OAuth support.
- `pooler preflight` sends no inference request and reports `inference_requests_sent: 0`, so it is always safe to run.

## Task prompts

Prompts a user can paste into a coding agent. Full text in the agent protocol.

- [Pool accounts with failover](docs/agent-native.md#pool-several-accounts-with-failover): add a second account and pool it so requests fail over on a rate limit.
- [Switch the active account](docs/agent-native.md#switch-which-account-is-active): inspect accounts and switch which one serves traffic.
- [Investigate slow requests](docs/agent-native.md#investigate-slow-or-failing-requests): read latency, TTFT, retries, and cooldowns from the management API.
- [Diagnose a broken setup](docs/agent-native.md#diagnose-a-broken-setup): run `doctor` and `preflight` and repair what is safe to repair.
- [Migrate from CLIProxyAPI](docs/agent-native.md#migrate-from-cliproxyapi): dry-run a legacy configuration, then write a validated one.
